observations.probe_scope: Installed native NVFP4 E2M1 group16 operators; deterministic random weights, FP32 dequantized reference, changed-input CUDA-graph replay, actual TP2 gate/up, down and output dimensions at M=1/4/8/128. No production monkey-patch, JIT build or host compilation.
findings: The generic QPN4 dispatcher rejects M1 K5120/N17408 gate/up and K3072/N5120 output with invalid split_k for K.
TP2 down K8704/N5120 M1 is numerically finite and graph-stable in this probe, and is faster: TurboMind59.2707us versus QPN4 40.4710us. This is a narrow candidate, not whole-model acceptance.

The same down route at M4 regresses from56.2067us to369.5350us; at M8 from56.1085us to372.4659us. Current QPN4 large-M dispatch dequantizes into a dense workspace rather than retaining the native TurboMind route.

Every successful changed-input graph replay matched its eager operator output exactly. Maximum QPN4-vs-FP32 absolute error across admitted probes was0.00154543, and maximum QPN4-vs-TurboMind absolute difference was0.001953125. These are operator-level observations, not an end-to-end model quality claim.
The installed bounded QPN4 workspace is5120*8704 FP16 elements. TP2 gate/up requires5120*17408, twice that capacity. Broadening shape guards without workspace/layout work is unsafe.

The accepted compressed-tensors QPN4 route explicitly gates max_num_seqs=1 and no MTP. ModelOpt global scales are direct multipliers, unlike the reciprocal compressed-tensors representation. No AWQ or compressed-tensors scale logic was copied into ModelOpt.

The faster M1 down-only candidate lacks complete checkpoint, mixed-prefill/concurrent-graph and long-output safety proof; it remains staged as evidence, not enabled. Its M4+ regression makes unconditional promotion unsuitable for the requested four-sequence service.
